summary: Alaska DEED urges the FCC to strengthen child‑protection safeguards under CIPA while preserving local flexibility, setting clear objectives, and avoiding unfunded or impracticable mandates. The DEED comments argue for flexible, locally‑driven E‑Rate policies that emphasize child safety, privacy, and meaningful parental engagement while avoiding blanket federal mandates on screen‑time, device ownership, and monitoring. They call for network‑level safeguards, reasonable supervision, and age‑appropriate digital‑citizenship education. DEED argues for preserving E‑Rate support for Alaska libraries, cautions against burdensome new CIPA rules, and calls for local flexibility in screen‑time and privacy policies. The Alaska Department of Education and Early Development urges the FCC to preserve local flexibility in internet safety, distinguish educational from recreational screen use, protect student privacy, set technically feasible standards for personally owned devices, recognize libraries’ distinct role, and avoid unfunded mandates while maintaining E‑Rate’s mission.
